description: Ground truth questions and answers for RAGAS evaluation based on TNAU and ICAR guidelines

questions.question: What are the best rice varieties in Tamil Nadu?
questions.ground_truth_answer: Popular rice varieties in Tamil Nadu include ADT 49, ADT 50, Co 51, and BPT 5204 (Ponni rice). These varieties are well-adapted to local conditions and have good disease resistance. ADT varieties are recommended by TNAU for their high yield and pest resistance.
ground_truth_contexts: ADT 49 is a high-yielding rice variety with good disease resistance recommended for Tamil Nadu
BPT 5204 Ponni rice is a premium variety suited for Tamil Nadu conditions
Co 51 variety has moderate disease tolerance and is suitable for local conditions

questions.question: When to sow rice in Kuruvai season?
questions.ground_truth_answer: Kuruvai season rice is typically sown from June to July. The ideal time is mid-June to early July. Seeds should be sown 25-30 days before transplanting. Seedlings are ready for transplanting in July-August. The maturity period is 90-100 days, with harvest in September-October.
ground_truth_contexts: Kuruvai rice seeds are sown in mid-June to early July
Seedlings require 25-30 days to become ready for transplanting
Kuruvai rice has a 90-100 day maturity period with September-October harvest

questions.question: What is the spacing for rice planting?
questions.ground_truth_answer: Recommended spacing for rice is 20-25 cm between rows and 10-15 cm between plants. For mechanical transplanting, spacing should be 20 cm x 15 cm. Higher densities reduce yields due to increased pest incidence. Line transplanting with recommended spacing gives better yields.
ground_truth_contexts: Row spacing of 20-25 cm is recommended for optimal rice yields
Plant spacing of 10-15 cm within rows prevents overcrowding
Mechanical transplanting uses 20 cm x 15 cm spacing for maximum efficiency

questions.question: What nitrogen dose is recommended for rice?
questions.ground_truth_answer: Standard nitrogen recommendation for rice is 60 kg/ha for high-yielding varieties. Apply nitrogen in three splits: 25 kg/ha at transplanting, 25 kg/ha at maximum tillering, and 10 kg/ha at heading. Soil nutrient status and expected yield should guide final dosage. TNAU recommends 60 kg N for 4 t/ha yield target.
ground_truth_contexts: Total nitrogen dose of 60 kg/ha is recommended for rice cultivation
Apply 25 kg N at transplanting as basal dose
Apply 25 kg N at maximum tillering stage for better panicle development
Apply 10 kg N at heading stage to promote grain filling

questions.question: How to control fungal blast in rice?
questions.ground_truth_answer: Fungal blast control involves: (1) Use resistant varieties like ADT 49 and ADT 50, (2) Maintain proper drainage to avoid waterlogging, (3) Avoid excessive nitrogen application, (4) Spray Tricyclazole 75 WP (1.2 g/L) during early infection, (5) Use Mancozeb (2.5 g/L) as preventive spray. Drain fields after symptom appearance.
ground_truth_contexts: Resistant varieties ADT 49 and ADT 50 are effective against fungal blast
Proper field drainage prevents fungal blast by reducing humidity
Tricyclazole 75 WP fungicide is effective when sprayed at early infection stage at 1.2 g/L
Mancozeb 75% WP at 2.5 g/L is used as preventive spray
Excessive nitrogen increases disease susceptibility in rice

questions.question: What is the water requirement for rice?
questions.ground_truth_answer: Rice requires 1000-1500 mm of water during the entire growing season. This includes rainfall and irrigation. Optimal water management includes continuous flooding at 5-7.5 cm depth up to soft dough stage. Alternate wetting and drying (AWD) can save 20-30% water. Drain fields 15-20 days before harvest.
ground_truth_contexts: Total water requirement for rice is 1000-1500 mm for the season
Maintain 5-7.5 cm water depth from transplanting to soft dough stage
Alternate wetting and drying conserves water and reduces input costs
AWD saves 20-30% irrigation water without reducing yields

questions.question: What is the temperature requirement for rice cultivation?
questions.ground_truth_answer: Rice grows best at 20-40°C temperature range. Optimum temperature for germination is 30°C. For vegetative growth, 25-30°C is ideal. During panicle initiation and flowering, 20-25°C is beneficial. Temperatures below 15°C affect seed germination. Frost damage occurs below 0°C.
ground_truth_contexts: Rice grows in temperature range of 20-40°C
Optimum germination temperature for rice is around 30°C
Vegetative growth is most vigorous at 25-30°C temperature
Panicle initiation and flowering benefit from cooler temperatures of 20-25°C

questions.question: How to control pests in cotton?
questions.ground_truth_answer: Major cotton pests are bollworms and aphids. Control measures: (1) Use resistant varieties, (2) Cultural practices like summer plowing and crop rotation, (3) Monitor pheromone traps (4-5 traps/acre), (4) Spray Spinosad 45% EC (350 mL/acre) or Endosulfan 35% EC for bollworms, (5) Spray Imidacloprid for aphids. IPM approach recommended.
ground_truth_contexts: Bollworms and aphids are major cotton pests requiring integrated management
Resistant cotton varieties provide first line of defense against pests
Pheromone traps at 4-5 traps per acre help monitor bollworm populations
Spinosad 45% EC at 350 mL/acre is effective against bollworms
Imidacloprid insecticide controls cotton aphid populations

questions.question: What is the fertilizer dose for sugarcane?
questions.ground_truth_answer: Recommended fertilizer for sugarcane: 150 kg N, 60 kg P2O5, 40 kg K2O per hectare. Apply nitrogen in 3 splits: 50% at planting, 25% at 4 months, 25% at 8 months. Phosphorus and potassium applied at planting. Bagasse ash application can save 25% potassium requirement.
ground_truth_contexts: Standard sugarcane fertilizer recommendation is 150 kg N per hectare
Phosphorus application is 60 kg P2O5 per hectare
Potassium requirement for sugarcane is 40 kg K2O per hectare
Apply 50% nitrogen at planting, 25% at 4 months, and 25% at 8 months

questions.question: How to control red rot in sugarcane?
questions.ground_truth_answer: Red rot is caused by Colletotrichum falcatum. Control: (1) Use resistant varieties like CoC 671, (2) Treat seed cane with Carbendazim 50% WP (2 g/L) for 30 minutes, (3) Remove infected plants and burn debris, (4) Avoid waterlogging, (5) Maintain field sanitation. No effective chemical control post-infection.
ground_truth_contexts: Red rot resistance varieties like CoC 671 prevent disease occurrence
Seed cane treatment with Carbendazim 50% WP at 2 g/L for 30 minutes prevents red rot
Infected plants should be removed and burned to prevent disease spread
Waterlogging increases red rot severity and should be avoided
Field sanitation is essential for red rot management in sugarcane
